title: "Tools: audio"
description: "The agent tools that detach and attach a clip's sound, normalise it, set it up for speech, match it to a reference and line clips up by their sound."
---

These tools work on a clip's sound as a whole: split it off, set its level, set it up for speech, match it to another clip, or line clips up by what they hear. For single settings, use [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).

`normalize_clip`, `enhance_voice`, `match_audio` and `sync_audio` measure sound, so they share three things:

- **They take no `scope`.** They work in whatever nest `set_scope` has open. To work inside a nest, open it first. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
- **They can take seconds**, and longer on a long clip. `enhance_voice` and `match_audio` render a clip to measure it, and so does `normalize_clip`'s loudness mode for a clip with processing.
- **They give up if the project changes meanwhile.** Nothing changes, and the answer says to call again.

All four are one undo step, and a second identical call changes nothing.

## `detach_audio`

Splits a clip's sound onto its own clip on the track below. It's **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (<kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>), see [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Look the clip up inside this nest. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

The original keeps its picture with its audio switched off. The new clip plays the sound with its video switched off. When the clip is on the bottom track, a new track is added under it.

The two are linked, and each names the other under `linked`. Moves, splits, ripples, nests and copies keep them in step. To make a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/), use `trim_start` or `trim_end` with `alone: true` on the sound. Speed and reverse edits are refused until [`attach_audio`](#attach_audio).

**Answers** with `new_clips` and, when one was added, `new_tracks`, then the [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).

**Refuses**, saying why, a clip that isn't a media clip, media with no audio, a clip whose audio is off (which is also what an already detached clip reads as), and a sound clip that would overlap a clip on the track below.

## `attach_audio`

Merges a detached pair back into one clip. It's **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** (<kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd>), see [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | Yes | Either half of the pair. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Look the clip up inside this nest. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

The picture's audio comes back on with the sound clip's audio settings, and the sound clip goes. Its track stays.

**Answers** with the project summary.

**Refuses** a clip that isn't linked, and a pair that no longer covers the same time, such as a J-cut or L-cut. Trim them to match first.

## `normalize_clip`

Sets each clip's volume so its loudness, or its loudest moment, lands on a target. It's the **Normalize** button in the Clip tab's **Volume** section and **Clip ▸ Normalize**, see [Normalize](/audio/normalize/). Those follow the mode chosen in the section's **Normalize** row. The tool doesn't read that row: it goes by its own `mode`.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
| `mode` | string | No | `loudness` takes each clip's integrated loudness to `target_lufs`, under a −1 dBTP ceiling. `peak` takes each clip's loudest moment to `peak_db`. Default: `loudness`, or `peak` when you give `peak_db` and no mode. |
| `target_lufs` | number | No | Loudness mode only. The loudness to land at, −50 to −5 LUFS. Default: −16. −14 is YouTube's playback reference and −23 is EBU R 128's. |
| `peak_db` | number | No | Peak mode only. Where the loudest moment lands, −60 to 0 dBFS. Default: −1. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

The level is measured before the clip's fader, over the part of the clip that plays. It knows nothing of the volume, fades, ducking, mute or solo already on the clip, because it's about the material, not the mix. That has three results:

- It **replaces** the volume rather than multiplying it, so a second call answers "made no change".
- It writes the clip's base volume, even with the playhead inside an action.
- It leaves `muted` alone.

In peak mode each clip gets its own gain to the same peak, so levels aren't matched across a selection. In loudness mode each clip goes to the one target, which does match them.

The volume can't go past 32×, so a clip quieter than about −31 dBFS can't reach −1. It's still normalised as far as it goes, and the answer says where it landed.

In loudness mode:

- A clip whose true peak would pass −1 dBTP at the target, or that already has a limiter, gets the clip's [limiter](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#compressor-and-limiter) in the same edit. Its own is kept with the ceiling at −1 dBTP at most, otherwise it's the default.
- A clip with an active EQ, hum notch, voice isolation, noise reduction, gate, leveller, de-esser, compressor or voice effect is measured through that processing, rendered offline as the export plays it. It waits for any isolation or voice render.

**Answers**, in peak mode, `peak_db` and a `normalized` list:

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
| `measured_db` | The clip's measured peak. |
| `volume` | The volume written. |
| `result_db` | Where the peak lands. |
| `clamped` | True when the 32× ceiling stopped it short. |

**Answers**, in loudness mode, `target_lufs`, `ceiling_dbtp` and a `normalized` list:

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
| `measured_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp` | The **Volume** section's Loudness readout. For a rendered clip the true peak is the processed one. |
| `processed_lufs` | The loudness through the clip's processing. `null` for a clip measured without a render. |
| `renders` | The renders it took. 0 for a clip measured without one. |
| `volume` | The volume written. |
| `limiter` | The clip's limiter after the edit, or `null` for a volume alone. |
| `result_lufs` | Where the clip lands. |
| `result_true_peak_dbtp` | Its true peak after the edit, held at the limiter's ceiling. |
| `limited_by` | `max_gain` when the volume ceiling stopped it short, otherwise `null`. |

Either mode adds `skipped`, one sentence per clip it left out, and `note` when the ceiling stopped a clip short. The rest are still normalised.

**Skips** by name a clip that plays no sound and a nest. Peak mode also skips one that's silent over the part that plays, or whose waveform hasn't been analysed yet. Loudness mode also skips one that plays under 0.4 s, is under −70 LUFS over the part that plays, or whose loudness hasn't been measured yet. In loudness mode a clip with processing is also skipped when its reversed copy is still being made, its processing can't be rendered, or it's under −70 LUFS after it. When every clip is skipped, the call fails with "Nothing could be normalised" and every reason.

**Refuses** a `target_lufs` or `peak_db` out of range, and either one in the other's mode. Neither is clamped.

## `enhance_voice`

Sets each clip up for speech from its own measurements. It's **Clip ▸ Enhance Voice** and the **Enhance Voice** button in the Clip tab's **Volume** section, see [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/). Those use the **Normalize** row's target and show the Measuring Sound sheet while they work.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
| `target_lufs` | number | No | The loudness each clip should land at, −50 to −5 LUFS. Default: −16. −14 is YouTube's playback reference and −23 is EBU R 128's. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload.

It measures the clip before any of its settings, then writes ordinary settings you can see and change in each section:

| Setting | When | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EQ | Always | The **Rumble Cut** high-pass, 80 Hz at 24 dB/octave. The EQ's other slots stay. |
| Voice isolation and gate | When the pauses' floor is less than 45 dB under the clip's loudness | Isolation at 0.8, or noise reduction at 0.5 where isolation can't serve the clip (a speed other than 1, a ramp or a freeze). The gate opens 10 dB above the pauses' median true peak, held to −40 to −6 relative to the loudness. With quiet pauses all three are off, and with under 0.5 s of pause they're left as they are. |
| Leveller | When the speech's short-term loudness range is over 6 LU | The leveller at its defaults, otherwise off. With under 3 s of speech it's left as it is. |
| De-esser | When at least 5% of the speech has its 6 kHz band within 10 dB of the loudness | The de-esser at its defaults, otherwise off. |
| Compressor | Always | 3:1 at the speech's median true peak, with makeup that gives back what it takes. |
| Limiter | Always | The clip's own, with its ceiling at −1 dBTP at most, otherwise the default. |
| Volume | Always | What takes the clip to `target_lufs`, solved on the clip rendered through these settings. |

It overwrites only `eq`, `isolation`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `volume`. Hum, channels, pan, mono, fades, ducking and mute stay. It writes base settings even with the playhead inside an action.

[`normalize_clip`](#normalize_clip) at the same target afterwards changes nothing, because it measures a processed clip the same way.

**Answers** `target_lufs`, `ceiling_dbtp` and an `enhanced` list:

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
| `measured_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp` | The clip's loudness and true peak, before its settings. |
| `speech_seconds` | How much speech it found. |
| `floor_lufs`, `floor_gap_db`, `pause_peak_dbfs` | The pauses' floor, its gap under the loudness, and their median true peak. |
| `sibilance_share` | The share of the speech that's sibilant. |
| `speech_range_lu` | The speech's short-term loudness range. `null` under 3 s of speech. |
| `set` | Exactly the keys written, in `set_audio`'s spelling. |
| `reasons` | One sentence per rule: the measurement, the threshold and what it set. |
| `volume`, `processed_lufs`, `renders` | The volume written, the loudness through the new settings before it, and the renders it took. |
| `result_lufs`, `result_true_peak_dbtp`, `limited_by` | Where the last render lands, and `max_gain` when the volume ceiling stopped it short. |

It adds `skipped` and `note` as `normalize_clip` does. A second call answers "Enhance Voice made no change".

**Skips** by name a clip that plays no sound, is a nest, plays under 0.4 s, is under −70 LUFS, or has under 1 s of speech. So too a clip whose loudness or speech hasn't been analysed yet, whose reversed copy is still being made, whose processing can't be rendered, or that's under −70 LUFS after its processing. When every clip is skipped, the call fails with "Nothing could be enhanced" and every reason.

**Refuses** a `target_lufs` out of range. It isn't clamped.

## `match_audio`

Gives clips the loudness and speech tone of a reference clip. It's **Clip ▸ Match Audio…**, see [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/), whose sheet picks the reference among the selected clips and has a **Loudness** and an **EQ** box.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reference` | integer | Yes | The clip whose loudness and tone the others take. It isn't changed. |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change. At least one. |
| `loudness` | boolean | No | Match the loudness, through the volume and limiter. Default: true. |
| `eq` | boolean | No | Match the tone, through the EQ's shelves and bands. Default: true. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload.

The reference is rendered once as it plays, with its settings, limiter and volume but no fades, ducks or mute, and its loudness is read.

**Loudness** is [`normalize_clip`](#normalize_clip)'s loudness mode at that target for every clip. It sets the volume, and the limiter when the peaks need it, solved on the clip rendered through its new settings.

**EQ** renders each clip with its shelves and bands off, keeping its high- and low-pass. Both clips' average spectra are measured over their speech only, needing about 1 s of it, in 23 third-octave bands from 79 Hz to 12.7 kHz. The difference between them, with the overall level taken out, is fitted by the EQ's low shelf, three bands and high shelf, with gains within ±12 dB and Q from 0.5 to 4. A band is used only where the difference is at least 0.5 dB. These replace the clip's own five, its high- and low-pass and hum stay, and `bypass` goes off.

It writes only `volume`, `limiter` and `eq`, as base settings even inside an action.

**Answers** `reference` (its `clip`, `media`, `lufs` and `speech_seconds`), `target_lufs` and a `matched` list:

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
| `set` | Exactly the keys written. |
| `eq`, `eq_fit_rms_db` | The fitted EQ, and how far it is from the difference in dB RMS. |
| `volume`, `measured_lufs`, `processed_lufs`, `result_lufs`, `result_true_peak_dbtp`, `limited_by` | The same figures as `normalize_clip`. |
| `renders` | The renders it took. |

It adds `skipped` and `note` as `normalize_clip` does. A second call answers "Match Audio made no change".

**Refuses** a call with `loudness` and `eq` both false, and a reference that plays no sound, is a nest, plays under 0.4 s, is under −70 LUFS, hasn't been analysed yet or, with `eq`, has under 1 s of speech.

**Skips** a clip that can't be matched for one of those reasons, or that is the reference. The rest are still matched.

## `sync_audio`

Lines clips up by their sound. One clip, the anchor, stays where it is. Every other clip moves along its own track by a whole number of frames, so its sound plays at the same moment as the anchor's. It's **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**, see [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to line up. At least two, each on its own track. |
| `anchor` | integer | No | The clip that stays put, one of `clips`. Default: among the clips with pictures (all of them when none has), the earliest start, then the rearmost track, then the lowest id. |
| `accept_weak` | boolean | No | Apply a weak match. Default: false. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

The matching runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload. The menu item leaves out a nest or a clip that plays no sound, where the tool stops and names it.

### How a match is chosen

Each file's sound is compared on features that ignore gain, microphone and room. When both stretches hold at least 2 s of speech, only their speech is compared. The clips' played windows are searched first, and the whole files only when that chooses nothing and a clip is trimmed.

- A **confident** match has a confidence of at least 10 and is 1.5 above the next candidate.
- A **weak** match is the best peak within 3 s of where the clip already sits, with a confidence of at least 4.

Either kind must then pass a check on the waveforms, which needs a clear peak within ±48 ms. A match that fails it is refused as not one recording, because features alone can match two takes of similar words.

See [Confident and weak matches](/audio/weak-sync-matches/).

### Apply a weak match

A weak match that would move anything isn't applied. The answer is `moved: false`, with `weak` naming the clips, each row's move and a `note`, and nothing changes.

:::caution
Pass `accept_weak: true` only after the person has agreed to that move, naming it. A weak match can be unrelated sound.
:::

### What it does to a clip

- **A clip that would start before 0** is trimmed at its head by that much and starts at 0. The anchor never moves or trims.
- **Clock drift** between the two recordings is measured over at least 60 s of overlap and corrected with a tiny speed change, as a resample. It's left alone when it's under 5 ms, under 3× its uncertainty, or would need a speed more than 0.2% from ×1, and `drift_note` says why.

### What it answers

An answer that isn't a refusal has `anchor`, `moved`, `weak` (the clip ids of weak moves) and a `synced` list. A second call answers `moved: false` and "already in sync".

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
| `offset` | Anchor source minus clip source at the overlap's centre, refined, in ticks. |
| `coarse_offset` | The match before the waveform refinement. |
| `refined`, `refine_confidence` | `phat` when the waveform check refined it, otherwise `coarse`, and that check's confidence, or `null` when none ran. |
| `delta`, `start` | How far the clip moves, and its new start. |
| `confidence` | How strong the chosen match is. |
| `search` | `played` or `whole`. |
| `chosen_by` | `confidence`, or `placement` for the weak tier. |
| `matched_on` | `speech` or `sound`. |
| `candidates` | Each search's candidates, as `offset`, `delta` and `confidence`. |
| `trimmed` | The ticks cut off its head, 0 when none. |
| `speed` | The clip's speed after the call. |
| `drift_ppm`, `drift_ms`, `drift_error_ms` | The drift measured and its uncertainty. |
| `drift_on`, `drift_windows` | `features` or `phat`, the points the drift line went through, and how many windows it used. |
| `drift_corrected`, `residual_ms`, `drift_note` | Whether it was corrected, the error left, and why not. |

### When it refuses

It's all or nothing: when any clip can't be matched, nothing moves and every reason is named. When no match is chosen, the sentence gives each search's candidates as the move each would make and its confidence, so you can move the clip near one and call again.

A clip can't be matched when it:

- is a nest, or plays no sound
- is still being analysed
- holds under 2 s of sound
- plays more than 0.2% away from ×1, plays at a rate other than its speed, plays reversed, or has a speed ramp
- shares a track with another of the clips
- would be left with under a frame after its head trim
- would never play beside the anchor, or would overlap another clip on its track

`anchor` must be one of `clips`.

---
title: "Tools: clean-up"
description: "The agent tools that find silences and filler words as ranges, make a filler transcript, and cut what they found."
---

These tools find what [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) would cut. The two `detect_` tools change nothing, so you can read and adjust their ranges before making the cut.

Neither `detect_` tool takes `scope`. They work in whatever nest `set_scope` has open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).

## Cut what the tools found

Pass the `ranges` from `detect_silence` or `detect_fillers` to [`ripple_delete_ranges`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_ranges). That's what **Remove** does in each sheet, and it makes the whole cut one undo step.

```json
{ "ranges": [[1200000, 1500000], [3000000, 3240000]] }
```

An agent isn't held to the ranges it was given: it can drop some or change them first. `ripple_delete_ranges` takes `scope` like any edit, so it can reach a nest without opening it. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).

## `detect_silence`

Finds the quiet stretches of the timeline and reports them, changing nothing. It's the read half of **Clip ▸ Remove Silences…**, see [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/).

The voice model runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | No | Analyse only these clips, like the sheet's **Selected clips**. At least one. Default: the current selection when it holds anything with sound, otherwise every audible clip. |
| `mode` | string | No | `voice` judges by the voice model, falling back to level over a clip that holds no voice. `level` judges by level alone. Default: `voice`. |
| `voice_confidence` | number | No | Voice mode only. The model's probability, 0.1 to 0.9, at or above which a moment counts as speech. Default: 0.5. The sheet doesn't offer this. |
| `threshold_db` | number | No | Quieter than this counts as silence, in dBFS in the mix, at or below 0. Default: −40. |
| `min_length` | integer | No | The shortest quiet run worth cutting, in ticks. Default: 300,000 (0.5 s). |
| `padding` | integer | No | How much to leave at each end of a run, in ticks. Default: 60,000 (0.1 s). |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

`min_length` and `padding` run exactly as sent. Only the finished ranges go on the frame grid, and they snap inward, which can leave a frame of room tone rather than clip the next word. Each takes 0 to 9,000,000,000,000,000.

Quiet is measured in the mix, so a clip's volume, fades, ducking, mute and another track's solo all count. In either mode, a moment the mix alone turns down to `threshold_db` or below is quiet.

A moment no clip in scope covers isn't a candidate, because a hole in the timeline isn't dead air. A nest clip is a wall: no range reaches into one.

**Answers:**

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `ranges`, `count`, `removes` | The spans as `[from, to]` pairs in ticks, how many, and how many ticks they remove. |
| `scope`, `clips` | `selected` or `audible`, and the clips that ran. This `scope` is about clips, not nests. |
| `mode`, `threshold_db`, `min_length`, `padding`, `voice_confidence` | What actually ran. |
| `judged_by_level`, `judged_by_level_clips` | The media and the clips judged by level because they hold no voice. |
| `proposed_by_mix_clips` | Each clip a range is proposed inside only because the mix turns it down while its analysis is still running. |
| `pending_peaks` | Media still being analysed, for either the waveform or speech. Call again shortly. |
| `voice_pending` | Media whose speech is still being analysed. |
| `protected_nests` | Each nest clip a quiet run of at least `min_length` crossed. There may be dead air inside. |
| `note` | Sentences on any of the above. |
| `project` | The [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/). |

`proposed_by_mix_clips`, `pending_peaks`, `voice_pending`, `protected_nests` and `note` appear only when they have something to report. To look inside a protected nest, open it with `set_scope` and call again.

**Refuses:**

- `voice_confidence` in level mode, or outside its range.
- `mode: "voice"` when the voice model can't be used. Leave `mode` out instead and it falls back to level with a note.
- A `threshold_db` above 0.
- A `min_length` or `padding` that's negative or too long.

See [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/).

## `detect_fillers`

Finds the filler words in the timeline's speech and reports them as ranges, changing nothing. It's the read half of **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**, see [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/).

The fillers it knows are ah, er, erm, hm, hmm, huh, m, mhm, uh, uh-huh and um.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | No | Read only these clips. At least one. Default: the current selection when it holds a clip with speech from a media file, otherwise every clip. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

It reads only a cached AssemblyAI transcript that asked for filler words, and never uses the network. It needs no key.

Each run of fillers is widened outward to a 32 ms grid, never into the words beside it, then its edges snap inward to the frame grid.

**Answers:**

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `ranges`, `count`, `removes` | The merged spans as `[from, to]` pairs in ticks, how many, and how many ticks they remove. |
| `fillers` | Each kept run, with its `clip`, `words` and `range`. |
| `dropped` | Each run left in, with its `clip`, `words` and `reason`. |
| `needs_transcript` | Media with no such transcript. [`transcribe_for_fillers`](#transcribe_for_fillers) makes one. |
| `locked` | Clips on a locked track, which weren't read, because `ripple_delete_ranges` neither cuts nor moves a locked track. |
| `scope`, `clips` | `selected` or `all`, and the clips that ran. |
| `skipped` | When you named `clips`, each one it couldn't read, with the reason. |
| `note` | Sentences on any of the above. |
| `project` | The project summary. |

A filler is dropped whole when:

- it's too short once it's on both grids
- it overlaps a word of another clip on any unlocked track, because the cut reaches every unlocked track, in scope or not
- it crosses a nest clip
- it crosses a transition

## `transcribe_for_fillers`

Re-transcribes one media file with AssemblyAI so its filler words can be found. It's the **Transcribe** button beside a file in **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**, see [Filler transcripts](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/).

:::caution
This is a paid upload to AssemblyAI, even over a transcript that's current for captions. It needs your AssemblyAI key, and the built-in Assistant can't use this tool.
:::

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | integer | Yes | The media to transcribe, one of `detect_fillers`' `needs_transcript`. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

It keeps the media's previous request (its language, speaker labels and vocabulary) and adds filler words. A media with no previous request gets language detection, no speakers and no vocabulary.

It writes only the media's transcript cache: no caption is placed and no undo step is made.

A media that already has a transcript made with filler words makes no request and needs no key. It answers `ready: true` and an empty `uploaded`.

**Answers:**

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `ready` | Whether `detect_fillers` can now read the media. |
| `media` | The media id. |
| `uploaded`, `cached` | The media uploaded, and the media answered from the cache. |
| `audio_seconds` | The seconds of audio billed. |
| `engine`, `language` | `assemblyai`, and the language code or `auto`. |
| `note` | Present when there's something to say. |
| `project` | The project summary. |

**Refuses:**

- A document with nowhere to keep its transcript cache. Save it first.
- A media no clip plays from its file.
- With no key, where it would upload: "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription."

Three things follow, and each is a decision rather than an accident. ---
title: "Tools: tracks, markers and canvas"
description: "The agent tools that add, reorder and set up tracks, place and change markers, and change the project's canvas."
---

These tools change the three things a project's clips sit in: the track stack, the markers on the ruler and the canvas. Each call that changes something is one undo step.

Track `index` 0 is the back of the layer stack, the bottom lane of the timeline. A higher index draws in front. Ids come from [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/), and times are ticks, 600,000 to the second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).

## `add_track`

Adds an empty track. It's **Track ▸ New Track** (<kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd>, see [New Track](/timeline/manage-tracks/#new-track)), except that an agent can choose where in the stack the track goes. The menu item always adds at the front.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | integer | No | Where in the stack, from 0 at the back to the track count at the front. Default: the front. |
| `name` | string | No | The track's name, such as `Titles`. Spaces at either end are dropped. Default: `Track` and the new count, so `Track 4` when there were three. A name of only spaces counts as no name. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Add the track inside this nest. `index` then counts that nest's own tracks. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

**Answers** with `new_tracks`, holding the new track's id, and the [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).

**Refuses** an `index` past the front, naming the range. A project holds at most 64 tracks, and that limit counts the tracks in every nest as well as the timeline's.

## `remove_track`

Removes a track. It's **Track ▸ Remove Track**, see [Remove Track](/timeline/manage-tracks/#remove-track). Where the menu item asks in an alert before it removes clips, the tool never asks: it refuses until you pass `with_clips`.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track's id. |
| `with_clips` | boolean | No | Remove the track's clips too. Default: false. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Look the track up inside this nest. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

**Answers** with the project summary.

**Refuses** two things:

- The only track left. A project always keeps one, and `with_clips` doesn't get past this.
- A track that still holds clips, unless `with_clips` is true. The sentence names up to three of the clips, gives a count for the rest, and says to pass `with_clips: true`.

## `move_track`

Moves a track to a new place in the layer stack, sliding the tracks it passes the other way. It's dragging a track header, see [Reorder tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/#reorder-tracks).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track's id. |
| `index` | integer | Yes | Its new position, from 0 at the back to one less than the track count. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Look the track up inside this nest. `index` then counts that nest's own tracks. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

**Answers** with the project summary. A track that's already at `index` answers "made no change".

**Refuses** an `index` past the last track, naming the range.

## `set_track`

Changes a track's name, its four switches, its matte and its mix. Anything you leave out keeps its value.

The switches are the track header's toggles and **Track ▸ Hide Video**, **Mute Audio**, **Lock Track** and **Solo**, see [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) and [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). `volume` and `pan` are **Track ▸ Mix…**, see [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track's id. |
| `name` | string | No | The track's new name. Spaces at either end are dropped, and an empty name leaves the track unnamed. |
| `hidden` | boolean | No | Drops the track's picture from the composition. |
| `muted` | boolean | No | Silences the track's sound. |
| `locked` | boolean | No | Keeps every ripple, insert and range edit off the track. |
| `solo` | boolean | No | Silences every other track in the same container that isn't also soloed. Mute wins on a track that's both, and pictures aren't touched. |
| `matte` | string | No | `none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or `luma_inverted`. See [Track mattes](#track-mattes). |
| `volume` | number | No | The track's fader as a linear gain from 0 to 4, multiplying every clip's own volume on it. 1 is unity, 4 is +12.04 dB and 0 is silent. |
| `pan` | number | No | The track's balance, from −1 (left) to 1 (right). It's a constant-power balance after each clip's own pan, and a mono source isn't panned. |
| `compressor` | object | No | The track's compressor, or `null` for off. See [A track's compressor and limiter](#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter). |
| `limiter` | object | No | The track's limiter, or `null` for off. See [A track's compressor and limiter](#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter). |
| `scope` | integer | No | Look the track up inside this nest. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

A container is the timeline, or one nest's own tracks. `volume` and `pan` play through nests: a nested clip is affected by its own track and by the track of every nest clip around it.

**Answers** with the project summary. A call that sets what's already there answers "made no change".

**Refuses** a call that names none of the optional arguments, and a `volume` or `pan` outside its range. Neither value is clamped.

### Track mattes

`matte` makes a track cut the track directly behind it in its container, as **Track ▸ Matte** does. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/).

| Value | In **Track ▸ Matte** | What cuts the track behind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | **Off** | Nothing. It's an ordinary track again. |
| `alpha` | **Alpha** | The matte track's alpha. |
| `alpha_inverted` | **Inverted Alpha** | Its alpha, inverted. |
| `luma` | **Luma** | Its brightness. |
| `luma_inverted` | **Inverted Luma** | Its brightness, inverted. |

The matte track's clips aren't drawn, but they still sound. Where the matte track shows nothing, the track behind shows uncut. A back-most matte track, or one in front of another matte track, cuts nothing.

### A track's compressor and limiter

`compressor` and `limiter` are **Track ▸ Mix…**'s **Compressor** and **Limit peaks**, see [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/). They run on the track's sub-mix, after every clip, its volume and its pan, compressor first. The limiter's ceiling is on what the track hands the mix.

Each takes an object, and that object **replaces the whole setting**. A key you leave out takes its default, not the value the track had. This is the opposite of [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#set_audio), where objects merge. `null` clears the setting, and leaving the argument out keeps it.

| `compressor` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `threshold_db` | −60 to 0 dB | −18 |
| `ratio` | 1 to 20 | 3 |
| `attack` | 0 or more ticks | 6,000 (10 ms) |
| `release` | 0 or more ticks | 120,000 (200 ms) |
| `makeup_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 0 |

| `limiter` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ceiling_db` | −24 to 0 dBTP | −1 |
| `release` | 600 to 600,000 ticks | 60,000 (100 ms) |

An unknown key, a mistyped value or a value out of range is refused, naming the key.

- **Timeline tracks only.** A nest's tracks have no compressor or limiter, so either argument is refused inside a nest. The track holding a nest clip is that nest's bus.
- **Exact in every export.** The preview runs them approximately.
- **Measuring tools don't hear them.** Normalize, the Loudness readout, Enhance Voice and Match Audio all measure without the track's compressor and limiter.

## `remove_empty_tracks`

Removes every track that holds no clips. It's **Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks**, see [Remove Empty Tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/#remove-empty-tracks).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scope` | integer | No | Tidy this nest's tracks instead. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

When every track is empty, the back-most one stays, because a project always keeps one.

**Answers** with the project summary, or "made no change" when no track can go.

## `add_marker`

Adds a marker to the timeline. It's **Mark ▸ Add Marker** (<kbd>M</kbd>), see [Add a marker](/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker), with a name, a colour and a chapter setting available in the same call.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | integer | No | Where, in ticks. It's rounded to the project's frame grid, and a time before 0 becomes 0. Default: the playhead. |
| `name` | string | No | The marker's name. Default: `Marker` and the new count, so `Marker 3` when there were two. |
| `chapter` | boolean | No | Also make it a [chapter](/export/chapters/) of the exported file. Default: false. |
| `color` | string | No | A colour name such as `red`, not a hex string. See [Marker colours](/timeline/markers/#marker-colours). Default: red. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Published on the tool, but a nest has no markers, so naming one is refused. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

**Answers** with `new_markers`, holding the new marker's id, and the project summary.

**Refuses:**

- A frame that already has a marker. The sentence names that marker. Two markers can't share a frame.
- A project already at its limit of 1,024 markers.
- Any call while a nest is open, because a marker sits at project time and the times in that call would be the nest's. Leave the nest with `set_scope` and no arguments first. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).

## `set_marker`

Moves or renames a marker, or changes its colour or chapter setting. Anything you leave out keeps its value. It mirrors dragging a flag on the ruler and the marker's row in the Document tab, see [Move, rename and remove a marker](/timeline/markers/#move-rename-and-remove-a-marker).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `marker` | integer | Yes | The marker's id. |
| `time` | integer | No | The new time, in ticks. It's rounded to the project's frame grid, and a time before 0 becomes 0. |
| `name` | string | No | The new name. An empty name leaves the marker unnamed. |
| `chapter` | boolean | No | Make it a chapter of the exported file, or stop it being one. |
| `color` | string | No | A colour name. An empty string keeps the colour it has. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Published on the tool, but a nest has no markers, so naming one is refused. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

**Answers** with the project summary.

**Refuses** a call that names none of `time`, `name`, `chapter` and `color`, and a `time` on a frame another marker holds.

With a nest open, `time` is refused for the same reason as in [`add_marker`](#add_marker). `name`, `chapter` and `color` still work, and the answer lists the edit under `document_ops`.

## `remove_marker`

Removes a marker. It's **Delete** in the marker's row in the Document tab, see [Move, rename and remove a marker](/timeline/markers/#move-rename-and-remove-a-marker).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `marker` | integer | Yes | The marker's id. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Published on the tool, but a nest has no markers, so naming one is refused. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

**Answers** with the project summary. With a nest open it still works, and the answer lists the edit under `document_ops`.

## `set_canvas`

Changes the project's canvas, the fixed frame every clip is drawn into. Anything you leave out keeps its value.

It mirrors the **Canvas**, **Frame Rate** and **Appearance** sections of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/). See [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/), [Project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/), [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/), [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/) and [Blending](/hdr/blending/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | integer | No | Canvas width in pixels, 16 to 16,384. It must be even. |
| `height` | integer | No | Canvas height in pixels, 16 to 16,384. It must be even. |
| `rescale_clips` | boolean | No | Scale every clip's placement with the canvas, so a layout looks the same after a resize. Default: false. |
| `fps` | array | No | The frame rate as `[numerator, denominator]`, each a whole number of 1 or more: `[30, 1]`, `[30000, 1001]` for 29.97, `[24000, 1001]` for 23.976. A bare whole number such as `30` also works. |
| `background` | array | No | The colour behind every layer as `[r, g, b, a]`, four numbers from 0 to 1. |
| `fit_new_clips` | boolean | No | Give a new clip Fit scale when its source is bigger than the canvas. |
| `timecode_frames` | boolean | No | Show times as `HH:MM:SS:FF` rather than `HH:MM:SS.mmm`. |
| `output` | string | No | The project's dynamic range: `sdr` (Rec. 709, the default for a project) or `hlg` (HDR, Rec. 2100 HLG). |
| `blending` | string | No | How layers blend: `encoded` (the default for a project) or `linear` light. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Published on the tool, but a nest's size is fixed, so naming one is refused. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

**Answers** with the project summary, or "made no change" when the canvas already says what you sent.

**Refuses:**

- A call with nothing to change.
- A `width` or `height` that's outside its range or odd.
- An `fps` term that isn't a whole number from 1 to 4,294,967,295.
- A fractional bare `fps` such as `29.97`. The sentence gives the pair to send.
- A `background` that isn't exactly four numbers, or has a value outside 0 to 1. It isn't filled in or clamped.

With a nest open, the call applies to the document instead, and the answer lists it under `document_ops`.

**Resizing.** Without `rescale_clips`, clips keep their pixel positions. With it, each clip's `x` follows the width's ratio, its `y` the height's, and its `scale` the smaller of the two, so a layer that fitted the old canvas still fits the new one. Two things stay as they were: the end of a move or scale in an [action](/mcp/tools-animation/) keeps its old target, and the clips inside a nest don't change, because a nest keeps its own size.

**Changing the frame rate** moves every clip's start and length, every action's span and every marker to the new grid, on the timeline and inside nests. On a coarser grid, two markers can land on one frame. When they do, the first in the project's list stays and the other is dropped. A rate change isn't refused because two clips end up overlapping by a frame more.

**Changing `output`** keeps every grade's settings, and a chroma key keeps keying the colour it was picked on. A qualifier's ranges read the HLG signal, so re-pick them after switching.

**Changing `blending`** to `linear` makes a dissolve keep its brightness, and soft edges and glows come out brighter. Grades, keys and qualifiers read what they did.

---
title: "Tools: clip sound (set_audio)"
description: "The Sound tab's settings through one agent tool: volume, fades, ducking, pan, EQ, dynamics, voice isolation and voice effects."
---

One tool sets what the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)'s controls store. You name the clips and send a patch of what should change, and the rest of each clip's sound stays as it is.

## `set_audio`

Changes the base sound settings of one or more clips, as one undo step. Read them back with [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/), where they're under each clip's `audio`.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
| `patch` | object | Yes | The settings to merge. Each key is described below. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Look the clips up inside this nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

```json
{
  "clips": [12, 15],
  "patch": {
    "volume": 0.8,
    "eq": { "high_pass": { "frequency": 100 } },
    "gate": {}
  }
}
```

The patch follows the rules of [Patches](/mcp/patches/):

- A key you leave out keeps what's stored.
- `duck`, `compressor`, `limiter`, `eq` and each of its slots, `hum`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser` and `voice` are objects, and they merge key by key.
- `null` on one of those clears it, so `{"duck": null}` turns ducking off.
- An empty object turns `limiter`, `gate`, `leveller` or an EQ slot on at its defaults, so `{"limiter": {}}` adds the limiter.

**Answers** with the [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/). A patch that changes nothing answers "made no change".

**Refuses** a key it doesn't know, naming its path, and a value out of range, naming the key and the value you sent. Nothing is clamped. A clip with no sound settings, such as a text clip, is refused by id.

All times in the patch are ticks, 600,000 to the second.

### Volume and mute

| Key | Type | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `volume` | number | The clip's gain, from 0 to 32. 1 is unity. |
| `muted` | boolean | Mutes the clip. |

See [Clip volume](/audio/volume/).

### Fades and fade shapes

| Key | Type | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fade_in`, `fade_out` | integer | The fade's length in ticks, 0 or more. |
| `fade_in_shape`, `fade_out_shape` | string | The fade's curve: `linear` (the default), `s_curve`, `plus_3db` for a fast start or `minus_3db` for a slow one. |

The shapes are the **Fades** section's **In shape** and **Out shape**. See [Audio fades](/audio/fades/).

### Ducking

`duck` lowers other sound while this clip plays, or only while its speech plays.

| `duck` key | Range | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | 0 to 1 | 0.2 | What the other sound is multiplied by. |
| `attack` | 0 or more ticks | 300,000 (0.5 s) | How long the sound takes to go down. |
| `release` | 0 or more ticks | 600,000 (1 s) | How long it takes to come back. |
| `mode` | `extent` or `speech` | `extent` | `extent` ducks for the clip's whole length. `speech` ducks only while its speech plays. |
| `pre_roll` | 0 or more ticks | 300,000 (0.5 s) | With `speech`, how far before each stretch of speech to start. |
| `hold` | 0 or more ticks | 300,000 (0.5 s) | With `speech`, how far after it to hold. |

`mode: "speech"` is **Speech** in the **Ducking** section's **Duck by** pop-up. It saves the media's detected speech in the same undo step, so it needs on-device speech detection to have finished. It's an error for a clip that isn't a media clip with sound, and for one whose speech hasn't been detected yet, which says to try again in a moment. To write the speech spans yourself, use `set_media_speech`.

See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) and [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).

### Mono, keep pitch, pan and channels

| Key | Type | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mono` | boolean | Plays the clip in mono. |
| `keep_pitch` | boolean | Keeps the sound's pitch at a new speed. A clip starts with this on. |
| `pan` | number | From −1 hard left to 1 hard right. |
| `channels` | string | `both` (the default), `left`, `right` or `swapped`. `left` and `right` play that channel of a stereo source from both sides, and `swapped` exchanges them. It comes after isolation and any voice effect, and a mono source ignores it. |

See [Pan and Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/), [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) and [Channels](/audio/channels/).

### Compressor and limiter

| `compressor` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `threshold_db` | −60 to 0 dB | −18 |
| `ratio` | 1 to 20 | 3 |
| `attack` | 0 or more ticks | 6,000 (10 ms) |
| `release` | 0 or more ticks | 120,000 (200 ms) |
| `makeup_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 0 |

`limiter` is a true-peak limiter, last in the clip's chain. Its ceiling holds after the clip's base volume.

| `limiter` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ceiling_db` | −24 to 0 dBTP | −1 |
| `release` | 600 to 600,000 ticks | 60,000 (100 ms) |

See [Compressor](/audio/compressor/) and [Limiter](/audio/limiter/). A track has its own pair, set with [`set_track`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter).

### Noise reduction and voice isolation

| Key | Range | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `noise_reduction` | 0 to 1 | Reduces noise in the clip's sound. |
| `isolation` | 0 to 1 | Isolates a voice with Apple's on-device model, which also reduces room echo. 0 is off, 0.8 is the app's default and 1 leaves silence between words. |

Isolation is rendered offline. The clip plays without it until the render lands, and an export waits for it. A clip not at ×1 plays without it.

See [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/).

### EQ

`eq` has seven slots, after the channel pick. Each slot is `null` for off, or an object.

| Slot | Keys | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `high_pass` | `frequency` 20 to 20,000 Hz, `slope` 12 or 24 dB/octave | 80 Hz, 12 |
| `low_shelf` | `frequency`, `gain_db` −24 to 24 dB | 100 Hz, 0 dB |
| `band_1`, `band_2`, `band_3` | `frequency`, `gain_db`, `q` 0.1 to 10 | 1,000 Hz, 0 dB, 1 |
| `high_shelf` | `frequency`, `gain_db` | 8,000 Hz, 0 dB |
| `low_pass` | `frequency`, `slope` | 12,000 Hz, 12 |

`bypass: true` keeps the settings and silences them. `{"eq": {"high_pass": {}}}` turns one slot on at its defaults.

The inspector's buttons are these moves:

| Button | Patch |
| --- | --- |
| **Rumble Cut** | `high_pass` at 80 Hz, slope 24 |
| **De-mud** | `band_1` at 300 Hz, −3 dB, Q 1 |
| **Presence** | `band_3` at 4,000 Hz, +3 dB, Q 1 |

See [EQ](/audio/eq/).

### Hum removal

`hum` notches out mains hum and its harmonics, after the EQ.

| `hum` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `frequency` | 50 or 60 Hz | 60 |
| `depth_db` | 6 to 60 dB | 30 |
| `harmonics` | 1 to 8 | 4 |

See [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/).

### Gate

`gate` is a downward expander after noise reduction that turns the pauses down. Below the threshold the level drops by the ratio less 1 dB for each dB, and never by more than `range_db`.

| `gate` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `threshold_db` | −40 to 0 dB, relative to the clip's measured loudness | −10 |
| `ratio` | 1 to 20 | 4 |
| `range_db` | 1 to 80 dB | 20 |
| `attack` | 0 to 60,000 ticks | 600 (1 ms) |
| `hold` | 0 to 300,000 ticks | 30,000 (50 ms) |
| `release` | 600 to 1,200,000 ticks | 60,000 (100 ms) |

The loudness it's relative to is what [`normalize_clip`](/mcp/tools-audio/#normalize_clip) reports, before the clip's volume. See [Gate](/audio/gate/).

### Leveller

`leveller` evens out a speaker who moves on and off the mic, after the gate. It's a gain curve made ahead of time from the clip's measured loudness and its speech, so it sounds the same in the preview and an export.

| `leveller` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target_db` | −20 to 10 dB, relative to the clip's loudness | 0 |
| `max_up_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 12 |
| `max_down_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 12 |
| `response` | 300,000 to 6,000,000 ticks | 1,200,000 (2 s) |

Each phrase's level is brought to `target_db`, never more than the two limits. A pause holds the gain and glides to the next phrase over its last 0.25 s, and a phrase under 1 s takes its neighbour's gain.

It waits for the clip's speech as well as its loudness. It does nothing where speech detection isn't available or no phrase has 1 s of speech. See [Leveller](/audio/leveller/).

### De-esser

`de_esser` comes after the leveller. It turns the band above `frequency` down on sibilance and never boosts it.

| `de_esser` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `frequency` | 2,000 to 12,000 Hz | 6,000 |
| `threshold_db` | −30 to 20 dB, relative to the clip's loudness | 0 |
| `range_db` | 1 to 24 dB | 6 |

The gate, leveller and de-esser act only once the clip's loudness is measured. Until then the clip plays without them, and an export waits. A clip too short or too quiet to measure plays without them, and on a nest clip they do nothing. See [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/).

### Voice effects

`voice` replaces the clip's sound with a rendered effect, after isolation and before the channel pick.

| `voice` key | Range | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | See below | None | Which effect. Needed when the clip has no voice effect yet. |
| `amount` | 0 to 1 | 1 | How much of the effect. 0 plays the clip dry. |
| `pitch` | −12 to 12 semitones | The kind's own: 0 for `pitch`, +5 for `high`, −5 for `deep` | Read only by `pitch`, `high` and `deep`. |

| Group | Kinds |
| --- | --- |
| Voice | `pitch`, `high`, `deep`, `robot` |
| Tone | `bass`, `treble`, `bright`, `telephone`, `radio` |
| Character | `lofi`, `distorted` |
| Space | `echo`, `room`, `hall`, `plate`, `cathedral` |

A new `kind` keeps a stored `pitch` unless you send `pitch: null` with it. `{"voice": null}` clears the effect.

The clip plays without the effect until its render lands, and an export waits for it. A clip not at ×1 plays without it, and reverb and echo tails end with the clip. See [Voice effects](/audio/voice-effects/).

## Animate sound

`set_audio` sets the clip's base values. To change one over time, use an action's `set_action_end`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/) and [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).

Volume, mute, the fades, `pan`, `mono`, `channels`, `eq`, `hum`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `isolation` can all animate. `duck`, `keep_pitch`, the fade shapes and `voice` can't, and only `set_audio` sets them.

---
title: "Tools: audio"
description: "The agent tools that detach and attach a clip's sound, normalise it, set it up for speech, match it to a reference and line clips up by their sound."
---

These tools work on a clip's sound as a whole: split it off, set its level, set it up for speech, match it to another clip, or line clips up by what they hear. For single settings, use [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/).

`normalize_clip`, `enhance_voice`, `match_audio` and `sync_audio` measure sound, so they share three things:

- **They take no `scope`.** They work in whatever nest `set_scope` has open. To work inside a nest, open it first. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
- **They can take seconds**, and longer on a long clip. `enhance_voice` and `match_audio` render a clip to measure it, and so does `normalize_clip`'s loudness mode for a clip with processing.
- **They give up if the project changes meanwhile.** Nothing changes, and the answer says to call again.

All four are one undo step, and a second identical call changes nothing.

## `detach_audio`

Splits a clip's sound onto its own clip on the track below. It's **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (<kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>), see [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Look the clip up inside this nest. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

The original keeps its picture with its audio switched off. The new clip plays the sound with its video switched off. When the clip is on the bottom track, a new track is added under it.

The two are linked, and each names the other under `linked`. Moves, splits, ripples, nests and copies keep them in step. To make a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/), use `trim_start` or `trim_end` with `alone: true` on the sound. Speed and reverse edits are refused until [`attach_audio`](#attach_audio).

**Answers** with `new_clips` and, when one was added, `new_tracks`, then the [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).

**Refuses**, saying why, a clip that isn't a media clip, media with no audio, a clip whose audio is off (which is also what an already detached clip reads as), and a sound clip that would overlap a clip on the track below.

## `attach_audio`

Merges a detached pair back into one clip. It's **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** (<kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd>), see [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | Yes | Either half of the pair. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Look the clip up inside this nest. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

The picture's audio comes back on with the sound clip's audio settings, and the sound clip goes. Its track stays.

**Answers** with the project summary.

**Refuses** a clip that isn't linked, and a pair that no longer covers the same time, such as a J-cut or L-cut. Trim them to match first.

## `normalize_clip`

Sets each clip's volume so its loudness, or its loudest moment, lands on a target. It's the **Normalize** button in the Clip tab's **Volume** section and **Clip ▸ Normalize**, see [Normalize](/audio/normalize/). Those follow the mode chosen in the section's **Normalize** row. The tool doesn't read that row: it goes by its own `mode`.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
| `mode` | string | No | `loudness` takes each clip's integrated loudness to `target_lufs`, under a −1 dBTP ceiling. `peak` takes each clip's loudest moment to `peak_db`. Default: `loudness`, or `peak` when you give `peak_db` and no mode. |
| `target_lufs` | number | No | Loudness mode only. The loudness to land at, −50 to −5 LUFS. Default: −16. −14 is YouTube's playback reference and −23 is EBU R 128's. |
| `peak_db` | number | No | Peak mode only. Where the loudest moment lands, −60 to 0 dBFS. Default: −1. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

The level is measured before the clip's fader, over the part of the clip that plays. It knows nothing of the volume, fades, ducking, mute or solo already on the clip, because it's about the material, not the mix. That has three results:

- It **replaces** the volume rather than multiplying it, so a second call answers "made no change".
- It writes the clip's base volume, even with the playhead inside an action.
- It leaves `muted` alone.

In peak mode each clip gets its own gain to the same peak, so levels aren't matched across a selection. In loudness mode each clip goes to the one target, which does match them.

The volume can't go past 32×, so a clip quieter than about −31 dBFS can't reach −1. It's still normalised as far as it goes, and the answer says where it landed.

In loudness mode:

- A clip whose true peak would pass −1 dBTP at the target, or that already has a limiter, gets the clip's [limiter](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#compressor-and-limiter) in the same edit. Its own is kept with the ceiling at −1 dBTP at most, otherwise it's the default.
- A clip with an active EQ, hum notch, voice isolation, noise reduction, gate, leveller, de-esser, compressor or voice effect is measured through that processing, rendered offline as the export plays it. It waits for any isolation or voice render.

**Answers**, in peak mode, `peak_db` and a `normalized` list:

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
| `measured_db` | The clip's measured peak. |
| `volume` | The volume written. |
| `result_db` | Where the peak lands. |
| `clamped` | True when the 32× ceiling stopped it short. |

**Answers**, in loudness mode, `target_lufs`, `ceiling_dbtp` and a `normalized` list:

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
| `measured_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp` | The **Volume** section's Loudness readout. For a rendered clip the true peak is the processed one. |
| `processed_lufs` | The loudness through the clip's processing. `null` for a clip measured without a render. |
| `renders` | The renders it took. 0 for a clip measured without one. |
| `volume` | The volume written. |
| `limiter` | The clip's limiter after the edit, or `null` for a volume alone. |
| `result_lufs` | Where the clip lands. |
| `result_true_peak_dbtp` | Its true peak after the edit, held at the limiter's ceiling. |
| `limited_by` | `max_gain` when the volume ceiling stopped it short, otherwise `null`. |

Either mode adds `skipped`, one sentence per clip it left out, and `note` when the ceiling stopped a clip short. The rest are still normalised.

**Skips** by name a clip that plays no sound and a nest. Peak mode also skips one that's silent over the part that plays, or whose waveform hasn't been analysed yet. Loudness mode also skips one that plays under 0.4 s, is under −70 LUFS over the part that plays, or whose loudness hasn't been measured yet. In loudness mode a clip with processing is also skipped when its reversed copy is still being made, its processing can't be rendered, or it's under −70 LUFS after it. When every clip is skipped, the call fails with "Nothing could be normalised" and every reason.

**Refuses** a `target_lufs` or `peak_db` out of range, and either one in the other's mode. Neither is clamped.

## `enhance_voice`

Sets each clip up for speech from its own measurements. It's **Clip ▸ Enhance Voice** and the **Enhance Voice** button in the Clip tab's **Volume** section, see [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/). Those use the **Normalize** row's target and show the Measuring Sound sheet while they work.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
| `target_lufs` | number | No | The loudness each clip should land at, −50 to −5 LUFS. Default: −16. −14 is YouTube's playback reference and −23 is EBU R 128's. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload.

It measures the clip before any of its settings, then writes ordinary settings you can see and change in each section:

| Setting | When | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EQ | Always | The **Rumble Cut** high-pass, 80 Hz at 24 dB/octave. The EQ's other slots stay. |
| Voice isolation and gate | When the pauses' floor is less than 45 dB under the clip's loudness | Isolation at 0.8, or noise reduction at 0.5 where isolation can't serve the clip (a speed other than 1, a ramp or a freeze). The gate opens 10 dB above the pauses' median true peak, held to −40 to −6 relative to the loudness. With quiet pauses all three are off, and with under 0.5 s of pause they're left as they are. |
| Leveller | When the speech's short-term loudness range is over 6 LU | The leveller at its defaults, otherwise off. With under 3 s of speech it's left as it is. |
| De-esser | When at least 5% of the speech has its 6 kHz band within 10 dB of the loudness | The de-esser at its defaults, otherwise off. |
| Compressor | Always | 3:1 at the speech's median true peak, with makeup that gives back what it takes. |
| Limiter | Always | The clip's own, with its ceiling at −1 dBTP at most, otherwise the default. |
| Volume | Always | What takes the clip to `target_lufs`, solved on the clip rendered through these settings. |

It overwrites only `eq`, `isolation`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `volume`. Hum, channels, pan, mono, fades, ducking and mute stay. It writes base settings even with the playhead inside an action.

[`normalize_clip`](#normalize_clip) at the same target afterwards changes nothing, because it measures a processed clip the same way.

**Answers** `target_lufs`, `ceiling_dbtp` and an `enhanced` list:

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
| `measured_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp` | The clip's loudness and true peak, before its settings. |
| `speech_seconds` | How much speech it found. |
| `floor_lufs`, `floor_gap_db`, `pause_peak_dbfs` | The pauses' floor, its gap under the loudness, and their median true peak. |
| `sibilance_share` | The share of the speech that's sibilant. |
| `speech_range_lu` | The speech's short-term loudness range. `null` under 3 s of speech. |
| `set` | Exactly the keys written, in `set_audio`'s spelling. |
| `reasons` | One sentence per rule: the measurement, the threshold and what it set. |
| `volume`, `processed_lufs`, `renders` | The volume written, the loudness through the new settings before it, and the renders it took. |
| `result_lufs`, `result_true_peak_dbtp`, `limited_by` | Where the last render lands, and `max_gain` when the volume ceiling stopped it short. |

It adds `skipped` and `note` as `normalize_clip` does. A second call answers "Enhance Voice made no change".

**Skips** by name a clip that plays no sound, is a nest, plays under 0.4 s, is under −70 LUFS, or has under 1 s of speech. So too a clip whose loudness or speech hasn't been analysed yet, whose reversed copy is still being made, whose processing can't be rendered, or that's under −70 LUFS after its processing. When every clip is skipped, the call fails with "Nothing could be enhanced" and every reason.

**Refuses** a `target_lufs` out of range. It isn't clamped.

## `match_audio`

Gives clips the loudness and speech tone of a reference clip. It's **Clip ▸ Match Audio…**, see [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/), whose sheet picks the reference among the selected clips and has a **Loudness** and an **EQ** box.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reference` | integer | Yes | The clip whose loudness and tone the others take. It isn't changed. |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change. At least one. |
| `loudness` | boolean | No | Match the loudness, through the volume and limiter. Default: true. |
| `eq` | boolean | No | Match the tone, through the EQ's shelves and bands. Default: true. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload.

The reference is rendered once as it plays, with its settings, limiter and volume but no fades, ducks or mute, and its loudness is read.

**Loudness** is [`normalize_clip`](#normalize_clip)'s loudness mode at that target for every clip. It sets the volume, and the limiter when the peaks need it, solved on the clip rendered through its new settings.

**EQ** renders each clip with its shelves and bands off, keeping its high- and low-pass. Both clips' average spectra are measured over their speech only, needing about 1 s of it, in 23 third-octave bands from 79 Hz to 12.7 kHz. The difference between them, with the overall level taken out, is fitted by the EQ's low shelf, three bands and high shelf, with gains within ±12 dB and Q from 0.5 to 4. A band is used only where the difference is at least 0.5 dB. These replace the clip's own five, its high- and low-pass and hum stay, and `bypass` goes off.

It writes only `volume`, `limiter` and `eq`, as base settings even inside an action.

**Answers** `reference` (its `clip`, `media`, `lufs` and `speech_seconds`), `target_lufs` and a `matched` list:

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
| `set` | Exactly the keys written. |
| `eq`, `eq_fit_rms_db` | The fitted EQ, and how far it is from the difference in dB RMS. |
| `volume`, `measured_lufs`, `processed_lufs`, `result_lufs`, `result_true_peak_dbtp`, `limited_by` | The same figures as `normalize_clip`. |
| `renders` | The renders it took. |

It adds `skipped` and `note` as `normalize_clip` does. A second call answers "Match Audio made no change".

**Refuses** a call with `loudness` and `eq` both false, and a reference that plays no sound, is a nest, plays under 0.4 s, is under −70 LUFS, hasn't been analysed yet or, with `eq`, has under 1 s of speech.

**Skips** a clip that can't be matched for one of those reasons, or that is the reference. The rest are still matched.

## `sync_audio`

Lines clips up by their sound. One clip, the anchor, stays where it is. Every other clip moves along its own track by a whole number of frames, so its sound plays at the same moment as the anchor's. It's **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**, see [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to line up. At least two, each on its own track. |
| `anchor` | integer | No | The clip that stays put, one of `clips`. Default: among the clips with pictures (all of them when none has), the earliest start, then the rearmost track, then the lowest id. |
| `accept_weak` | boolean | No | Apply a weak match. Default: false. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

The matching runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload. The menu item leaves out a nest or a clip that plays no sound, where the tool stops and names it.

### How a match is chosen

Each file's sound is compared on features that ignore gain, microphone and room. When both stretches hold at least 2 s of speech, only their speech is compared. The clips' played windows are searched first, and the whole files only when that chooses nothing and a clip is trimmed.

- A **confident** match has a confidence of at least 10 and is 1.5 above the next candidate.
- A **weak** match is the best peak within 3 s of where the clip already sits, with a confidence of at least 4.

Either kind must then pass a check on the waveforms, which needs a clear peak within ±48 ms. A match that fails it is refused as not one recording, because features alone can match two takes of similar words.

See [Confident and weak matches](/audio/weak-sync-matches/).

### Apply a weak match

A weak match that would move anything isn't applied. The answer is `moved: false`, with `weak` naming the clips, each row's move and a `note`, and nothing changes.

:::caution
Pass `accept_weak: true` only after the person has agreed to that move, naming it. A weak match can be unrelated sound.
:::

### What it does to a clip

- **A clip that would start before 0** is trimmed at its head by that much and starts at 0. The anchor never moves or trims.
- **Clock drift** between the two recordings is measured over at least 60 s of overlap and corrected with a tiny speed change, as a resample. It's left alone when it's under 5 ms, under 3× its uncertainty, or would need a speed more than 0.2% from ×1, and `drift_note` says why.

### What it answers

An answer that isn't a refusal has `anchor`, `moved`, `weak` (the clip ids of weak moves) and a `synced` list. A second call answers `moved: false` and "already in sync".

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `clip`, `media` | Which clip and file. |
| `offset` | Anchor source minus clip source at the overlap's centre, refined, in ticks. |
| `coarse_offset` | The match before the waveform refinement. |
| `refined`, `refine_confidence` | `phat` when the waveform check refined it, otherwise `coarse`, and that check's confidence, or `null` when none ran. |
| `delta`, `start` | How far the clip moves, and its new start. |
| `confidence` | How strong the chosen match is. |
| `search` | `played` or `whole`. |
| `chosen_by` | `confidence`, or `placement` for the weak tier. |
| `matched_on` | `speech` or `sound`. |
| `candidates` | Each search's candidates, as `offset`, `delta` and `confidence`. |
| `trimmed` | The ticks cut off its head, 0 when none. |
| `speed` | The clip's speed after the call. |
| `drift_ppm`, `drift_ms`, `drift_error_ms` | The drift measured and its uncertainty. |
| `drift_on`, `drift_windows` | `features` or `phat`, the points the drift line went through, and how many windows it used. |
| `drift_corrected`, `residual_ms`, `drift_note` | Whether it was corrected, the error left, and why not. |

### When it refuses

It's all or nothing: when any clip can't be matched, nothing moves and every reason is named. When no match is chosen, the sentence gives each search's candidates as the move each would make and its confidence, so you can move the clip near one and call again.

A clip can't be matched when it:

- is a nest, or plays no sound
- is still being analysed
- holds under 2 s of sound
- plays more than 0.2% away from ×1, plays at a rate other than its speed, plays reversed, or has a speed ramp
- shares a track with another of the clips
- would be left with under a frame after its head trim
- would never play beside the anchor, or would overlap another clip on its track

`anchor` must be one of `clips`.
